title: Fidelity Gap Injector and Surge Protocol
author: Asha Patel
content:
Summary
This page describes the Fidelity Gap Injector (FGI) — an internal test harness and procedural protocol used to simulate deliberate fidelity regressions and sudden request surges across the serving runtime. FGI is intended to validate: fidelity orchestration fallbacks, kernel scheduling robustness, KV-cache warmup behavior, SLO preservation under degraded model variants, and observability signal completeness for regression detection.

Use cases
- Validate that the fidelity orchestrator applies the intended degradation staircase (quantization variant -> reduced beam/length -> fallback model) without violating latency SLOs.
- Stress scheduler admission and preemption logic during synthetic microbursts and multi-tenant surges.
- Exercise profiling pipelines to ensure traces and sampling remain representative during fidelity transitions.
- Generate reproducible benchmark artifacts for capacity planning and Dedicated sizing.

High-level architecture
- Injector controller (service: fgi-controller): orchestrates experiments, schedules surge events, and applies fidelity knobs via the runtime control-plane API.
- Runtime adapter (lib: fgi-runtime-adapter): translates fidelity directives into ops: kernel hint mapping, model-variant pinning, KV-cache TTL adjustments, and admission weight updates.
- Traffic generator (tool: fgi-trafficgen): replays real request surfaces with the option to amplify entropy and sequence-length distributions.
- Observability hooks: automatic trace tags (fgi.experiment_id, fgi.phase, fgi.injected_gap) and bespoke metrics (fgi.slo_violation_count, fgi.kernel_preempt_events).

Design principles
1) Non-destructive by default: experiments run only against dedicated sandbox clusters or shadowed routes.
2) Determinism where possible: each run stores a reproducible seed, traffic signature, and a snapshot of the model-variant catalog used.
3) Cross-layer instrumentation: each fidelity transition must carry trace baggage so metrics and traces can be correlated to kernel events and scheduler decisions.

Configuration reference (sample experiment manifest)
| field | description | example |
|--|--|--|
| experiment_name | free text id | fidelity-gap-quant-then-surge-2026-01 |
| target_cluster | runtime target | sandbox-eu-west-1 |
| baseline_variant | model variant to start from | rdx-7b-fp16 |
| degrade_sequence | ordered list of fidelity stages | [r-dx-7b-int8,r-dx-7b-aux-short] |
| surge_profile | links to traffic profiles | microburst-100kqps-30s.json |
| slo_target | p99 latency target (ms) | 120 |
| kv_warmup | boolean: pre-warm kv caches | true |
| kernel_hint_map | optional map of kernel overrides | {"attention":"fast-path"} |

Note: the runtime control-plane accepts this manifest via POST /internal/v1/experiments and returns experiment_id for observability correlation.

Procedural runbook (quickstart)
1) Reserve sandbox resources: open ticket to infra-elect to provision sandbox-eu-west-1 for 4h. Include expected GPU class and capacity.
2) Prepare traffic: pick a seed corpus using fgi-trafficgen select-corpus --app=search --size=100k --seed=20250212.
3) Create manifest: copy template and set degrade_sequence, surge_profile, and slo_target.
4) Preflight checks (automated): POST /internal/v1/experiments/preflight - verify kernel hint compatibility and model variant availability. Abort if preflight fails.
5) Launch: POST /internal/v1/experiments -> record experiment_id. Monitor observability dashboard (dash: fgi-experiments/<experiment_id>).
6) Postmortem checklist: export traces (fgi.export-traces), run fidelity regression comparison (scripts/compare-fidelity-deltas --baseline=control-run --subject=run-<id>), and file experiment summary.

Profiling playbook for diagnosing failures during FGI runs
- Symptom: sudden p99 spikes during transition to quantized variant.
  1) Check trace baggage for fgi.phase and fgi.injected_gap.
  2) Correlate to kernel_preempt_events and kernel_queue_depth metric.
  3) Snapshot kernel selection logs: /var/log/kernel-mapper/selection.<timestamp>.log. Look for unexpected fallback to slow-path kernels.
  4) Compare GPU occupancy and tensor-core utilization across baseline vs injected run. If occupancy drops while CPU dispatcher shows high retries, suspect a compatibility regression in custom kernel.

- Symptom: KV-cache miss storm on surge after fidelity transition.
  1) Verify kv_warmup setting in manifest.
  2) Inspect kvcache.hit_rate and kvcache.load_latency by shard.
  3) If misses cluster on shard N, consult session-affinity map and eviction logs; consider increasing prefetch concurrency or temporary session affinity relaxation.

Benchmarking protocol (result artifacts and acceptance)
- Each experiment must produce: a) SLO burnup chart (p50/p95/p99), b) kernel-fidelity transition timeline, c) per-tenant token cost delta, d) trace sample set (min 500 traces with fgi tags).
- Acceptance criteria for merging an operator change that touched scheduler or kernel: no increase in p99 of >5% under identical FGI runs; no new kernel-fallback patterns observed more than 2x baseline frequency.

Release notes for tool and protocol (v1.3.0)
- Released 2026-02-18: first production-ready FGI with surge-profile orchestration and trace baggage contract.
- New metrics: fgi.kernel_preempt_events, fgi.slo_violation_count, fgi.kvcache_miss_burst_count.
- Runtime adapter now supports kernel_hint_map with per-kernel weight overrides (experimental).

Ownership and run cadence
- Primary owner: serving-runtime performance team (owner: Marcus Chen).
- On-call: runtime-experiment-rotation (1 week cadence) handles experiment scheduling and emergency aborts.
- Quarterly: run the standard FGI matrix across three representative catalogs (small chat, long-format summarization, high-entropy search) and upload results to capacity-planning.

Known issues and mitigations
1) Non-deterministic trace sampling in high-throughput surges: increase sampling quota using observability.rate_limit.override for experiment_id.
2) Kernel hint map compatibility: older kernels ignore hint weights and fall back silently — the adapter will emit kernel.map_compat_warning and the manifest preflight fails unless skip_compat_check is set. Avoid skip in normal runs.
3) Traffic generator can overdrive the ingress when misconfigured profiles are used; always run a short 15s smoke with --verify-backpressure to validate.

Safety & compliance constraints
- Customer data: FGI must never be run against production routes carrying customer PII. Use shadowed replay or sanitized corpora.
- Confidentiality: experiment artifacts that include request payloads must be stored in restricted buckets with kms key id: proj/key-fgi.

Operational integrations and examples
- Example kernel hint payload (YAML):
  kernel_hint_map:
    attention: fast-path
    matmul: energy-saver

- CLI example: fgi-controller submit --manifest=manifests/quant-surge-30s.yaml --cluster=sandbox-eu-west-1 --notify=#runtime-experiments

Diagnostics checklist (post-failure)
1) Export traces for experiment_id, tag: fgi.injected_gap.
2) Pull kernel mapper logs and scheduler decision trace for window [t0-60s, t0+300s].
3) Run automated fidelity delta analysis: tools/fgi/compute_delta --baseline control-run --candidate run-<id> --output=delta-report.json.
4) Open issue with label 'fgi-regression' and include artifacts: delta-report.json, sLO-burnup.png, trace-sample.tgz.

Appendix: standard surge profiles
- microburst-100kqps-30s.json: sharp ramp to 100k qps sustained for 30s, random inter-arrival jitter 0–2ms.
- ramp-10m-5min.json: linear ramp to 10m qps over 5 minutes to validate autoscale and admission smoothing.
- cohort-spike-tenantized.json: concentrated load on 3 tenants representing 80% of tokens, used to validate multi-tenant preemption and fairness.

FAQ
Q: Can I run FGI against Dedicated clusters?
A: Yes, but only with explicit capacity-owner signoff and during pre-approved maintenance windows; do not run without reserved capacity.

Q: Does FGI change real data?
A: No — by default we use shadow replay or sanitized corpora. Any run that must touch production data requires legal and security approval and must be marked 'restricted'.
